record.original_question: (M. Tărnăuceanu). Is it true that for every positive rational number r there exists a finite group G such that | Aut(G)|/|G| = r? A similar question is answered in the positive for graphs, monoids, partial groups, and posets(R. Molinier, Preprint, 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.21059). It is also known that the set {| Aut(G)|/|G| | G is a finite abelian group} is dense in [0, +∞) (M. Tărnăuceanu, Elemente Math. (2025), https://ems.press/journals/ em/articles/14298544).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite group $G$, let $\mathrm{Aut}(G)$ denote its automorphism group, and consider the rational number $|\mathrm{Aut}(G)|/|G|$. Prove or disprove: for every positive rational number $r$, there exists a finite group $G$ such that
\[
\frac{|\mathrm{Aut}(G)|}{|G|} = r.
\]
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed by M. Tărnăuceanu as a new entry in the 2026 Kourovka Notebook of unsolved problems in group theory. Related results are known: the set of ratios $|\mathrm{Aut}(G)|/|G|$ for finite abelian $G$ is dense in $[0,\infty)$ (Tărnăuceanu, Elemente Math., 2025), and analogous "every positive rational is realized" statements have been established for graphs, monoids, partial groups, and posets (Molinier, 2025). No solution for arbitrary finite groups has been located.

status_evidence.title: Density of automorphism-to-order ratios for finite abelian groups
status_evidence.snippet: The set {|Aut(G)|/|G| : G finite abelian} is dense in [0,∞).
status_evidence.claim: A density result is known for the abelian case, but realization of every positive rational by some finite group remains the open question.

status_evidence.title: R. Molinier, Preprint 2025
status_evidence.snippet: Analogous question answered positively for graphs, monoids, partial groups, and posets.
status_evidence.claim: Analogues are solved in related categories, supporting that the group case is the genuine open question.
